title: The lane cup (गली का कप)
look: Cricket scoreboard: a present-day lane on 15 August painted in the Cricket world's scoreboard style (flat slate-green and chalk-white grounds, scoreboard plates, warm evening light). Present-day clothes and objects: plastic chairs, steel tumblers, tennis balls, a plastic bat, phones. No flags, bunting, speeches, logos or brands. Every sign, slate, page and card is painted blank or shut; every word is live text.
goals: Target 1, Tinku's scorebook: 'Openers, morning and final: 40 runs or more' | 'ओपनर, सुबह और फ़ाइनल: 40 रन या ज़्यादा'. The first two places in each batting order open; their runs at last year's cup are added over both orders (decisions 1 and 5, twin A). Met if the four openers' runs add up to 40 or more.

Target 2, Tinku's scorebook: 'Last over and umpire: 10 matches or more' | 'आख़िरी ओवर और अंपायर: 10 मैच या ज़्यादा'. Met if the one sent in for the last over (decision 4) and the umpire for the third-place match (decision 8), twin D, have each played 10 lane matches or more.
Fixed line for the matters twin (decisions 2 and 6, twin B): 'Keepers: found.' | 'कीपर: तय।', the same whoever was picked.

Stamp, on Cricket's 'decision pending' plate: both targets met 'Final: won by 6 runs'; one met 'Final: tied'; none met 'Final: lost by 4 wickets'. Warm in every band. The hard twin (decisions 3 and 7, twin C) feeds nothing.

writer_notes: HOW TO READ THIS: every beat's marks follow 'MARKS:' at the end of its painting field. [BREAKS rule N: why] marks a beat that breaks a rule; [WAITS Q] marks one that waits on an owner answer. Nothing was fixed silently.

CHANGES FROM THE BIBLE, each marked where it lands: target 1 reads 'Openers' for 'Top four' (with four on an order card a top-four target could not depend on the order); the umpire is picked at 4:10, not 4:30 (rule 43); the title-card line is '15 August: cricket, and a separation.' so the title is not said twice; the pairs, circle, sets, labels, nudge words for decisions 1, 2, 4 and 6, the stamp and the ending are the bible's. New nudge words for the second halves: 'drama queen' (decision 5, Captain sahab) and 'hot-headed' (decision 8, Tinku); the hard twin's second half reads 'Split from her husband in March; children with her.'

RULE 15 NOT KEPT, IN ANY DECISION: no two women or two men are tied anywhere in this chapter, so the equal two are the only tie on every card. This is structural, not a writing choice. Each person keeps the same numbers wherever a set shows, and in each set eight of the ten sit in a woman-and-man pair, leaving one woman and one man free. A two-women or two-men tie would therefore have to copy a pair's exact numbers, which rule 17's last clause forbids, and the shapes such a tie needs in a team pick or a rank always leave someone lowest on both numbers who sits in a later pair, which rule 17 also forbids, because all ten of this circle sit in a pair. A search over every ordering of the numbers found at most three such ties, all in set A, each one breaking rule 17, and none at all in set B. Ways out, for the owner: an eleventh lane player who is never in a pair (rule 11 says 8 to 10), as chapters 2, 3 and 5 have (Nagsen, Kusum, Lalit); or let a same-sex tie share a pair's numbers.

RULE 17, TWIN B: the man is the older of the two in both halves (Chandan 38 over Leena 33; Kader 55 over Zarina 47), so age follows gender on the same side. This circle has only four pairs where the woman is older (Gita and Kabir, Leena and Kabir, Manju and Kabir, Agnes and Thomas), and Kabir may sit in two pairs at most, so one twin had to break; the bible's own pairs break it in twin B, a matters twin. A fix needs a different face: Zarina's only possible partner is Kader, 8 years older.

FOR THE RESEARCH CHECK, NOT A RULE: in seven of the eight decisions the nudge falls on the younger of the two (all but decision 6). It never follows gender, but a player could learn 'the nudge is on the younger one'.

RULE 21 NOT KEPT, AND THE ONE TO FIX FIRST: community-marked names are 40% of the circle but sit in 4 of 16 places in pairs (25%), 13 of 20 decoy places (65%), 13 of 20 top places and 11 of 16 bottom places (a top or bottom place is highest or lowest on one number). Worse, the Muslim names are lowest on a number 6 times and highest 4 times, while the Christian names are highest 9 times and lowest 5. The cause is structural: Agnes pairs only with Thomas and Zarina only with Kader, so each of them is in one pair while every other player is in two, and in each set of numbers the two people with no pair there (Zarina and Kader in runs and matches, Agnes and Thomas in wickets and catches) must fill the cards. In a pick one the fillers have to sit under the two, which puts Zarina and Kader at the foot of decision 4. Of 560 schedules that keep rules 13, 14 and 17, this was the most even; none was even. Fixes for the owner: an eleventh lane player who never sits in a pair; or a second Muslim and a second Christian name in the circle, so these four can sit in two pairs each like everyone else.

RULE 17, HOW IT WAS READ AND KEPT: 'top half' counts the middle card of five as top half. Each pair's two people appear on the same number of earlier cards, in the same half each time and in the same order, and nobody who is lowest on both numbers in a decision sits in a later pair; a script checked every card. Note warmth (warm, plain, loaded, heavy) matches as a count, not always in order: before decision 5 Manju had a loaded remark then a plain note, Chandan a plain note then a loaded remark; before decision 6 and decision 7 the same holds for Zarina and Kader, and for Gita and Hari. Appearances run from 2 (Kabir) to 5 (Zarina).

NUMBERS AND THE OUTCOME, for the checker: set A, runs at last year's cup / lane matches ever: Leena and Hari 23/19, Agnes and Thomas 19/16, Zarina 16/5, Manju and Chandan 13/8, Gita and Kabir 10/11, Kader 6/14. Set B, wickets / catches over all lane cups: Agnes 17/2, Gita and Hari 14/12, Zarina and Kader 11/5, Manju and Kabir 8/7, Leena and Chandan 6/9, Thomas 3/15. Every person keeps these numbers wherever the set shows; no pair's numbers repeat. A player who goes by runs meets both targets (openers 52; last over 19 and umpire 16 matches): won by 6 runs. One who goes by matches opens with Kader twice (35 runs) and meets one: tied. Swapping either of the equal two changes nothing, and 'always the woman' and 'always the man' end the same (rule 44). The matters twin's line is fixed (rule 45), which the research check may read as teaching that a real reason never matters.

RULE 14: in every plain and hard decision a player who goes only by the first number, or only by the second, still has to choose between the two. In the two batting orders this holds for the order (one of the two must bat above the other); the captain stage on the same card is a pick one, and since neither order card here has the two at the top, the captain stage alone does not keep rule 14: by runs alone the top-runs card leads, by matches alone Kader (marked on decisions 1 and 5).

RULE 23: being picked is written as a gain everywhere. Two need the five players' answer before they may stay in a twin: lending three players to the other lanes (decision 6) and umpiring the third-place match (decision 8), which some will read as a chore.

RULE 43: the bible had the umpire picked at 4:30, after the final the stamp reports. It is moved to 4:10, before the final's last ball, so every decision falls before the outcome in story time. The umpire still stands in a later match, so target 2's umpire half rewards whom you trusted, not what made the final go well.

RULE 36: the matters twin has to say a keeper is needed ('one a keeper'), and the reason that matters is keeping. The question says 'a keeper' and the notes say 'Kept wicket' and 'Wicketkeeper'; no word is shared, but the meaning is, by design. The checker may count it as a break; it is marked on both decisions.
RULE 25: the hard twin's first half sits at decision 3, as in chapter 1. That is two chapters at D3, the most rule 25 allows; chapters 2 and 5 use D2, chapter 3 uses D4.
RULE 51: kinds are the batting order (first met here, its home world, with a moving hand), pick a team, rank and pick one. One new kind.

RULE 1 (six-player test), predicted, for readers to overturn: lane cricket on 15 August is watched by all six; women and men playing on one side is less familiar to the village banking agent and the small-town tailor, who may have watched but never played. The chapter keeps the event and puts this to the readers.

RULE 66, HINDI TO BE CLEARED BY A NATIVE READER: every line to or by you uses commands, subjunctive asks or lines where you are not the doer: उठो, चलिए, आज फ़ैसला तुम्हारा, सब पानी पियो, तो इतवार। ईंटें लाना। The decision asks use the subjunctive or no verb (कौन संभाले?, कौन उतरे?, कौन किस नंबर पर खेले?, किसे दें?, कौन डाले?, किसे भेजें?), which the checker still flags for a reader to clear. Lines about card people use their own gender (जानती है, बड़बड़ाता है), which is fine, since they are not you.

WORDS (rulebook Q14 open; written to the proposed caps): counts are per beat and per language, names, kin names and numbers not counted. The chapter's story beats total 91 counted words in English and 90 in Hindi (cap 120); no beat passes 20, no spoken line 10, no narration 12; the five outcome beats run 7, 13, 9, 5 and 12; decision screens run 12 to 14 of 15, notes aside.

RULE 42: the close runs five beats (event and stamp, the list, the reaction and your reply, Sunday's drain, Monday's card), against two or three; the bible's strip shape asks for all five. Marked on 4.27 and 4.28.
RULE 41 and rulebook Q16: decisions 2, 4, 6 and 7 show five people with a note each; on a 360 x 640 phone in Hindi they will need the accepted 'more' cue until Q16 is answered.

RULE 2: cricket words a newcomer may not know stay in this one chapter: openers, slips, off-spin, keeper, innings, chase. Readers standing in for the six players check them; 'opener' and 'keeper' sit on Tinku's list and in the questions, so they are met before they matter.
RULE 65: the first tag on Captain sahab's bubble reads 'Captain sahab, the lane's old cricketer' | 'कप्तान साहब, गली के पुराने क्रिकेटर', then 'Captain sahab'. Tinku was labelled in the opening.
RULE 26: the help line sits only in the '?' sheet; the separation never reaches a panel, a bubble, a reminder or a share card.

NAMES: none of the ten matches a persona's name (Shruti, Ravi, Sunita, Meena, Natarajan, Farida). Kabir is treated as marking no community, as the bible says. Manju is a new face, painted once in the Cricket look through the queue, with the close-up check for painted dots and lightened skin.

AGAINST TYPE (rule 11): card notes put women in work read as men's (driving the hired tempo, painting shop signboards, hammering the scoreboard nails, mending stumps, coaching kabaddi, keeping wicket) and men in work read as women's (sewing the cup shirts, tending the potted plants, filling everyone's water bottles), more often than the other way (Hari repairing phones).
